title: OpenAI’s chief scientist has thoughts on how to limit AI development

claims.claim: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki published a blog post discussing potential limits on AI development.

evidence.quote: A new blog post from OpenAI’s chief scientist Jakub Pachocki discusses potential limits on AI development, with a focus on a measurement called perplexity.

claims.claim: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman described Jakub Pachocki's post as the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while.

evidence.quote: Pachocki’s post — described by Altman as “the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while” — suggests perplexity (not to be confused with the company of the same name) could be that measurement.

Pachochki’s post — described by Altman as “the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while” — suggests perplexity (not to be confused with the company of the same name) could be that measurement.

claims.claim: Jakub Pachocki suggested perplexity could be used as a measurement for AI progress.

evidence.quote: Pachocki’s post — described by Altman as “the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while” — suggests perplexity (not to be confused with the company of the same name) could be that measurement.
With perplexity serving as a standard measurement for AI progress, the companies would commit not to go past a certain threshold...

claims.claim: Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token on average, where lower perplexity means better predictions.

evidence.quote: perplexity — which “measures how well a model predicts the next token on average; lower perplexity means better predictions” — has remained “informative.”

claims.claim: Jakub Pachocki's post includes a chart showing how the perplexity of OpenAI's models has fallen since GPT 3.5.

evidence.quote: Pachochki’s post includes a chart of how the perplexity of OpenAI’s models has fallen since GPT 3.5.

claims.claim: GPT-4 achieved a perplexity score of approximately 0.91.

evidence.quote: “GPT‑4, at ~0.91, was proficient at utilizing chain-of-thought reasoning productively
“GPT‑4, at ~0.91, was proficient at utilizing chain-of-thought reasoning productively...

claims.claim: Losses below 0.8 have led to the emergence of transformative capabilities in fields like cybersecurity and mathematics according to Jakub Pachocki.

evidence.quote: “Now, as we have reached losses below 0.8, we have seen the emergence of transformative capabilities in fields like cybersecurity and mathematics.”
